slides.title: Run Your Territory Like a Business
bullets: Decide deliberately who deserves sustained attention and who doesn't
Decide which interactions genuinely need to happen in person
The opposite of a reactive calendar that just fills up

slides.title: Map the Full Landscape First
bullets: Understand every institution, investigator and emerging expert
Not just the names already familiar from handover notes
Connects directly to KOL segmentation and mapping in Module 3

slides.title: Build a Prioritised Engagement Plan
bullets: Decide which relationships need quarterly in-person contact
Which can run on lighter-touch virtual engagement
Which are emerging opportunities worth early investment
Identify where evidence-generation priorities meet the map

slides.title: Logistics That Make Field Work Sustainable
bullets: Travel planning and congress calendars
Balancing time so no region gets neglected for months
Protecting unscheduled time to properly process insights
Deployment decisions are strategic, not just logistical

slides.title: Review the Plan on a Fixed Cadence
bullets: Review quarterly against what actually happened
Ask whether engagement matched the plan
Ask whether new insights should reshape next quarter
Territory ownership is continuous, not a one-time onboarding task

takeaway.title: Owning a territory means running it as a deliberate, evolving strategy
bullets: A good map of who matters and why comes before any engagement plan
The plan balances in-person, virtual and emerging relationships
It gets reviewed and updated on a fixed cadence, not left to go stale
